entries.note: Plural; listed separately because pt gets no endings. Same figurative collision as aposta.
Bettor. Almost always gambling in the Brazilian press and feeds.
Plural bettors. Used heavily in the news about the betting law.
Casino. Rare ordinary uses: a city name, a beach in Rio Grande do Sul (Cassino), the film.
Plural of cassino.
Brazilian slang for a betting site ('as bets', 'bet liberada'). Collides with the BET channel, 'bet' as English slang for yes, and the name Bet; whole word only.
Plural slang, 'as bets'. Rarely ordinary; whole word only so no stray stem match.
Card game. Rare ordinary use (a candy, a film).
Casino card game, also the crystal brand Baccarat; rare in feeds. Brazilian spelling bacara is too rare to list.
Lottery. Collides with figurative 'a loteria da vida' and 'ganhar na loteria' as a wish.
Caixa lottery game, name always about the lottery.
Caixa lottery game.
Single-word form of Mega-Sena, the main Brazilian lottery; the two-word form is a phrase.
Scratch card. In some regions also the name of a shaved-ice treat.
Slang for the Fortune Tiger slot, huge in Brazil since 2023. Also a pet name or a small tiger.
The Aviator crash game. Also an English word and sunglasses style; Portuguese 'aviador' is a different word and is not matched.
Betting odds, used as an English loanword in Brazilian betting talk. Rarely ordinary in pt.
Top prize. Also used loosely: 'ganhei na sorte, foi um jackpot'.
Gambling addiction. A mention of it is a mention of gambling.
'Fazer uma fezinha' is to place a small bet, usually on a lottery or the bicho. Rare in other senses.
Operator of the jogo do bicho. Ordinary sense is almost nil.
Betting house, the standard term for a bookmaker.
Plural of the above.
Tiger game, the best-known slang of the market. Covered by tigrinho too; kept so the reason shown can be exact.
Illegal animal lottery, a Brazilian tradition.
Crash game 'little plane'. The single word aviaozinho is left out because it also means a drug courier in slang and a toy plane.
Two-word form of Mega-Sena. Hyphen splits to two tokens, so the hyphenated form is caught here.
Slot machine ('caca-niquel'); the hyphen splits tokens so this matches both forms.
Plural of caca-niquel.
Game of chance, the legal term for gambling in Brazil.
Plural of the above; frequent in news on the betting law.
Sports betting, the market's own category name.
Free bet, a bookmaker promotion.
No-deposit bonus, a typical bookmaker and casino hook.
Free spins, the Portuguese term. Rarely ordinary.
English form of free spins, used as-is in Brazilian ads.
Boosted odds, a promotion type. The singular and the word 'turbinada' are not listed because turbinada alone is ordinary.
The slot behind the tiger craze.
Sister slot from the same studio, promoted as the ox game.
Sister slot, the rabbit game.
Sister slot, the mouse game.
Sister slot, the dragon game.
Slot studio whose name appears in the same promos.
Slot and casino studio, appears in the same promos.
Major Brazilian bookmaker, football shirt sponsor.
Bookmaker with heavy influencer promotion in Brazil.
Global bookmaker, strong in Brazil.
Bookmaker with large sports sponsorship in Brazil.
Crash and casino site very visible in Brazil. Ordinary English word, and a stem of blazer, blazing; whole word only.
Long-running bookmaker in Brazil.
Brazilian bookmaker.
Bookmaker known for fast Pix withdrawals.
Betting exchange, used in Brazil.
Brazilian bookmaker, sports sponsor.
Bookmaker with heavy advertising.
Bookmaker with heavy influencer ads.
Global bookmaker with a Portuguese-language presence.
Global bookmaker active in Brazil.
Bookmaker active in Brazil.
Global bookmaker with Brazilian football deals.
Online casino built for the Brazilian market.
Brazilian bookmaker.
Bookmaker advertised heavily in Brazil. Short, so whole word only; also an Spanish and Polish word elsewhere.
Bookmaker with major sports sponsorship.
The two-word form is gambling; replaces the bare slot and slots entries that were rejected.
Online poker for money; replaces the bare poker entry that hit the poker face joke.
Portuguese spelling (pôquer) with accents folded; the bare word collides with the idiom cara de pôquer, the phrase does not.
Singular of apostas esportivas; the bare aposta was rejected, so the singular needs this phrase.
Singular betting phrase used in ads and news about the betting law.
Verb form with online; covers the infinitive in betting talk without the figurative apostar.
Free spins in the Brazilian wording (giros grátis), common in ads for Fortune Tiger and similar slots.
Caixa lottery game, always about the lottery.
The year-end special Mega-Sena draw, a big lottery topic every December.
Caixa lottery game tied to football clubs.
Person with gambling addiction; ludopatia does not match it by stem, ludopatas is covered by this entry.
Two-word spelling of the brand, widely used in posts; estrelabet is already listed.
Brand name is written as three words in its own ads; vaidebet is already listed.
Two-word spelling of betnacional.
Bookmaker active in Brazil with football sponsorship.
Bookmaker aimed at Brazil and Latin America.
Bookmaker with heavy influencer promotion in Brazil.
Bookmaker advertised in Brazil.
Brazilian bookmaker.
Global bookmaker with Portuguese-language ads in Brazil.
